questions.question: Why do scientists observe the similarities and differences in the features of organisms?
options: To determine how fast they can run.
To classify them into groups within larger groups.
To predict their future evolutionary traits.
To estimate their average lifespan.

questions.question: Which of the following shows the correct order of classification from the broadest group to the most specific?
options: Kingdom down to species
Species down to kingdom
Genus down to kingdom
Phylum down to domain

questions.question: Compared to a smaller classification group like a genus, a larger group such as a kingdom contains:
options: Fewer organisms with more similarities in their features.
Fewer organisms with fewer similarities in their features.
More organisms with more similarities in their features.
More organisms with fewer similarities in their features.

questions.question: What defines a group of organisms as belonging to the same species?
options: They live in the same habitat and eat the same food.
They have similar features and genes, and can reproduce to make fertile offspring.
They look identical and have the exact same body temperature.
They are able to survive in any environment on Earth.

questions.question: In the binomial system of naming organisms, what two levels of classification do the names represent?
options: Kingdom and Phylum
Genus and Species
Class and Family
Order and Genus

questions.question: Besides visible external features, how do scientists classify organisms at a microscopic level?
options: By the color of their external shell or skin
By studying their characteristics at the cellular level
By measuring their overall body weight
By observing how they interact with other animals

questions.question: Which of these is a common cellular feature that can help distinguish plants from animals?
options: Plants have cells with cell walls made of cellulose, while animal cells lack cell walls.
Animals have cells with chloroplasts, while plant cells do not.
Plants have prokaryotic cells, while animals have eukaryotic cells.
Bacteria and animals both have cells with nuclei containing DNA.

questions.question: If a scientist discovers a multicellular organism with cell walls made of chitin and no chloroplasts, which kingdom does it most likely belong to?
options: Plants
Animals
Fungi
Bacteria

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of using a classification key in biology?
options: To count the number of individuals in a population
To find out which groups organisms are classified into
To estimate the age of a specific organism
To measure the rate of photosynthesis in plants

questions.question: What does a classification key consist of to help identify an unknown organism?
options: A series of questions about the features of organisms
A list of all known scientific binomial names in alphabetical order
A set of instructions on how to dissect a specimen
A map showing where different species live around the world

questions.question: Why is biological classification important for scientists studying the Earth's ecosystems?
options: It helps us organise and make sense of biodiversity.
It allows us to control the weather in different biomes.
It guarantees that no more species will go extinct.
It helps us calculate the exact age of the Earth.

questions.question: When studying organisms in their natural habitat, what sequence of actions should a student perform?
options: Capture, keep, and domesticate the organisms.
Make, record, and interpret observations of the organisms.
Ignore, avoid, and bypass the organisms.
Genetically modify, breed, and release the organisms.

questions.question: While conducting fieldwork, what tool would be most useful to identify and classify an unfamiliar insect?
options: A classification key
A thermometer
A measuring tape
A weighing scale

questions.question: When carrying out ecological fieldwork, how should students conduct themselves?
options: Collect as many live specimens as possible to take home.
Work safely in a way that minimises harm to living organisms and disruption of ecosystems.
Clear away all vegetation in the study area to see the ground better.
Introduce new plant species to see how the local animals react.

questions.question: A horse and a donkey can mate to produce a mule, but mules are sterile and cannot reproduce. What does this tell us about horses and donkeys?
options: They belong to the exact same species.
They do not belong to the same species.
They belong to different kingdoms.
They do not share any common genes.
